why_angle: The cited StormWatts page and PowerSized work out price per Wh and refill hours only for EcoFlow, Jackery, Anker and BLUETTI kits, at November 8 prices or older. They list no ALLPOWERS kit and give no shipping state for most rows. This page shows that the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 + 400 W kit ships now at $0.48 per Wh with a 4.8 h rated-sun refill, and adds the maker's own 55–65% panel-output figure. It also corrects the Jackery 'Solar Generator 2000 v2' at $1,239: that kit carries 200 W of panels, and the 400 W version costs $1,649.

What the differences mean

Dealectric does not test units. The figures below come from the makers' US stores, read 2026-11-17, and from the named reviewers given beside each number.

  • Price per Wh is the price you pay divided by the rated battery. ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 + 400 W: $913.49 ÷ 1,920 Wh = $0.48. BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2 × 200 W: $1,424.05 ÷ 2,073.6 Wh = $0.69. Jackery Solar Generator 2000 v2: $1,239 ÷ 2,042 Wh = $0.61.
  • Hours of full sun to refill is the battery divided by the kit's panel watts, so it assumes the panels deliver their full rating. ALLPOWERS: 1,920 ÷ 400 = 4.8 h. BLUETTI 2 × 200 W: 2,073.6 ÷ 400 = 5.2 h. Jackery: 2,042 ÷ 200 = 10.2 h.
  • Real panel output is lower. ALLPOWERS's own listing says its polycrystalline SP037 panel gives about 55–65 W per 100 W. At 60%, 1,920 ÷ (400 × 0.6) = 8.0 h, so plan on more than one sunny day to refill from empty.
  • Usable energy. StorageReview measured 1,910 Wh from the Elite 200 V2: $1,424.05 ÷ 1,910 = $0.75 per measured Wh. OutdoorGearLab measured 1,710 Wh from the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2: $1,239 ÷ 1,710 = $0.72. No named lab has published a measured figure for the R2500 V2, so its $0.48 is per rated Wh.

Price per Wh and refill time for kits that ship now

The {buy:allpowers-r2500-v2-sp037-solar-kit} is the only 2 kWh-class kit under $1,500 that ships today with 400 W of panels. The $913.49 price uses the APBF12 code our link applies. That code passed a cart test on another ALLPOWERS product on 2026-11-17 but has not been tested on this kit. Without it, the store price is $1,038.05: $1,038.05 ÷ 1,920 = $0.54 per Wh, still under the budget. Bought as separate parts at store prices, the R2500 V2 ($649.00) plus the SP037 ($379.05) come to $1,028.05, $10 less than the kit's store price. ALLPOWERS rates the station for up to 1,000 W of solar, so there is room for a second panel later. The kit has a 5-year warranty.

Watch the Jackery name. Jackery's $1,239 'Solar Generator 2000 v2' is the Explorer 2000 v2 with two 100 W Air panels, 200 W in total. The version with two SolarSaga 200 W panels costs $1,649, which is over this budget.

If you can wait, the {buy:bluetti-elite-200-v2-2x200w-solar-kit} ships from Nov 26 and has the highest AC rating here, 2,600 W. Wire its two SP200L panels in series: 2 × 24.6 V = 49.2 V open-circuit, within the station's 12–60 V input. In parallel they reach 2 × 10.8 A = 21.6 A short-circuit, over the station's 20 A limit.

For cold climates: the ALLPOWERS R3500 manual and Anker's C2000 Gen 2 page both list a charging floor of 32°F. BLUETTI says the sodium-ion {buy:bluetti-pioneer-na-200w-solar-kit} charges at 5°F and runs loads down to −13°F.

Where the line was drawn: every row costs $1,500 or less at the price paid on 2026-11-17. The ALLPOWERS R3500 + 400 W kit rose to $1,803.10 at the store ($1,586.73 with the code), so it is left out. Anker's C2000 Gen 2 + 400 W bundle (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W) is marked sold out on Anker's US store, with shipping from early December. EcoFlow lists its DELTA 3 Max Solar Generator from $1,229. Its store page did not show which panel that price includes when we read it, so the kit is not in the table.

Not recommended

The ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + SP037 400 W kit looks cheap at $0.63 per rated Wh. StorageReview, however, measured only 920 Wh from the S2000 Pro at a 350 W load, and the unit switched off with 22% still showing. That works out to $917.93 ÷ 920 = $1.00 per measured Wh. The Solar Lab reported that the unit shut off at 55% battery under a 2,250 W load. Both tests used an earlier unit (StorageReview's dates from 2023). For about the same price, the R2500 V2 kit has more battery and the same 400 W panel.
